subject: BandPilot packaging: seat-pooling, burst credits & entitlement fencing
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Amir Khan <amir.khan@meditech.ai>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-21T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: BandPilot packaging: seat-pooling, burst credits & entitlement fencing

Hi Amir —

Great speaking earlier. Per our call, attached is a short workbook that lays out three packaging approaches that would let BandPilot (1) reduce committed seats for steady-state usage, (2) keep an on-demand burst pool for spiky events (e.g., campaigns), and (3) control which product features remain available when seats are reduced.

High level options in the workbook:
- Tiered core seats + pooled burst credits (recommended for uneven traffic)
- Elastic metering (pay-as-you-go with soft min commit)
- Hybrid: smaller commit + reserved burst capacity with feature flags for entitlements

Key asks from you:
1) Which option aligns best with your procurement timeline (commit vs payg)?
2) Rough target steady-state committed seats for Q3 (ballpark OK)
3) Any regulatory constraints around data residency for the burst pool?

I'll loop in Priyom and Karthik so we can put together a one-page amendment and a sample pricing table. If you want, we can sketch a canary migration that keeps the same SLAs for critical endpoints and gates lower-tier features behind entitlements.

Thanks —
Naomi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: Packaging_Options_Workbook.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Amir Khan <amir.khan@meditech.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@meditech.ai
Date: 2026-06-21T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BandPilot packaging: seat-pooling, burst credits & entitlement fencing

Thanks Naomi — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we bring legal in: 

1) In the pooled-burst model, can burst credits be shared across regions or do they have to be region-bound? We run campaigns in EU and US and prefer a single pool if possible.
2) If we reduce committed seats mid-quarter, how is pro-ration handled and can we reserve a minimum for core routing?
3) On entitlements: we need to ensure certain analytics endpoints (audit logs, recent inference traces) remain available to our ops team even on reduced seats. Can those be whitelisted?

Also — our procurement lead wants an initial delta number: what's the typical discount band for moving from full-commit to hybrid-commit (approx)? We understand it depends on volumes, but a ballpark range will speed internal conversations.

Best,
Amir
Head of Platform
Meditech AI
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: BandPilot packaging: seat-pooling, burst credits & entitlement fencing

Naomi / Karthik — forwarding Amir's notes. Suggested internal play:

- Recommend the hybrid model (smaller commit + reserved burst pool) — gives Meditech cost predictability while preserving campaign headroom.
- Pricing mechanics: propose a 20-30% discount on committed-seat unit price vs current list, plus a block of burst credits priced at ~40% of committed unit (billed monthly as reserved pool).
- Pro-ration: allow mid-quarter downsizes with a one-time admin fee (e.g., $500) and pro-rate the remaining commit for that quarter; next quarter starts at the new level.
- Entitlements: we can whitelist analytics endpoints. That will be implemented via a role-based entitlement toggle tied to the contract amendment.

Questions for Naomi: do we want to offer Meditech a 90-day trial of the burst pool (zero-cost) as a concession to close this quarter? It could be a lever to avoid a larger discount.

- Priyom

From: Amir Khan <amir.khan@meditech.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, contracts@meditech.ai
Date: 2026-06-23T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BandPilot packaging: seat-pooling, burst credits & entitlement fencing

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Priyom. A few follow-ups from procurement/ops: 

- Region pooling: EU-bound data must stay in EU for ~10% of requests due to partner rules. If the burst pool is global we need assurance that routing will respect regional residency for flagged flows. Can you confirm technical enforcement?
- Discount: 20-30% band looks reasonable; procurement wants to see two concrete scenarios (1) 25% commit discount + 30% priced burst pool, (2) 15% commit discount + free 60-day burst trial.
- Entitlement whitelist: operations will send a short list of endpoints that must remain available.

We can share the ops list tomorrow; once we have the two scenarios, I'll loop contracts and legal for the amendment.

Regards,
Amir
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-24T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BandPilot packaging: seat-pooling, burst credits & entitlement fencing

Thanks — quick plan of action so Naomi can send to Amir: 

1) Draft two clean scenarios in the workbook tab:
   a) Scenario A: 25% commit discount; burst pool priced at 30% of committed unit; 30-day trial of burst pool on sign-up.
   b) Scenario B: 15% commit discount; 60-day free burst trial; reserved burst pool at 40% pricing thereafter.
2) Call out enforcement for regional residency: burst routing will prefer regional pools; flagged flows will pin to EU nodes (we'll note implementation details for legal).
3) Entitlement gating: add a clause that up to 5 operational endpoints can be whitelisted; additional endpoints priced as an add-on.
4) I'll produce a 1-page amendment template (BandPilot_Amendment_draft_v1.docx) and Naomi can send to Amir + contracts.

Naomi — want to offer the 60-day trial in Scenario B as the public concession or keep that for final counter? My vote: present both and lead with Scenario A (leaner discount, smaller trial), surface B as a sweetener if legal pushes back.

—Karthik
